{{Elections in Georgia}}

The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the 14 [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], one from each of the state's [[Georgia's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[2022 Georgia gubernatorial election|Georgia gubernatorial election]], as well as other elections to the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|U.S. House of Representatives]], elections to the [[2022 United States Senate elections|U.S. Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]].

The 1st district is based in the Southeast corner of the state, encompassing Savannah and lower areas. {{see also|Georgia's 7th congressional district}}

The 7th district comprises suburbs and exurbs of [[Atlanta, Georgia|Atlanta]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[Carolyn Bourdeaux]], who has represented the district since 2021. She flipped the district and was elected with 51.4% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/> Bourdeaux is running for re-election. She faced a primary challenge from the [[Georgia's 6th congressional district|6th district's]] Representative [[Lucy McBath]], who opted to change districts after her current district was redrawn during redistricting to heavily favor the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. McBath easily won the primary and will face a Republican opponent in November.

The 14th district is based in the northwest corner of the state. Incumbent Republican [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]], who has represented the district since 2021, was elected with 74.7% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/> Greene is running for re-election, after winning a legal challenge to her eligibility based on her alleged involvement in organizing and promoting the [[2021 United States Capitol attack]], based on the [[Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution]], which bars people who have engaged in insurrection from serving in Congress.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-22 |title=Marjorie Taylor Greene's candidacy challenged at hearing |url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-biden-presidential-atlanta-525429753ace40f5b6e01ceab6f79549 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en}}</ref>
